collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: An elder can no longer read carvings up close, and a villager grinds glass discs: offer the glass, or wait to be asked.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has always been the one who could read the old carvings on the storehouse posts. Lately, the marks have gone fuzzy whenever (subject.he/she) brings them close. (subject.He/she) hasn't said anything. But (friend), who has been grinding glass from the black sand into smooth clear discs, has noticed (subject.him/her) squinting and holding things at arm's length.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) brings over two little polished discs set in a frame of bent cane, to hold up in front of the eyes. (subject) is doubtful. Then (subject.he/she) looks through them at the carvings, and goes completely silent. Every mark is sharp. (subject.He/she) reads the whole post aloud, slowly, the way (subject.he/she) used to. Then (subject.he/she) reads it again. (friend) pretends not to see (subject.him/her) wiping (subject.his/her) eyes.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (friend) says nothing. A week later, (subject) comes to (friend.him/her) at the glass fire and asks, gruffly, if those clear discs (friend.he/she) makes do anything useful. (friend) holds one up in front of (subject)'s eyes over a leaf, and (subject) sees the tiny hairs on it. They work on the frame together. It takes a few tries. It's worth it.
